query: Which clinical factors best explain longer visit durations?

per_column.name: visit_type_category
per_column.rationale: The type of visit (chronic followup, acute illness, wellness, emergency) plausibly drives both what clinical interventions occur (treatment-like factors) and the visit duration. It is a common upstream cause and was not named in the query.

per_column.name: condition_acuity
per_column.rationale: Acuity plausibly causes both whether procedures/admissions occur and how long the visit lasts. It sits upstream of the candidate causes and the outcome. Related to 'urgency' already in the table but surfaced here as a clinical severity variable; not restated in the query.

per_column.name: procedure_performed
per_column.rationale: A concrete candidate cause whose effect on duration is being attributed: performing a procedure directly lengthens a visit.

per_column.name: admission_or_urgent_referral
per_column.rationale: Admission/urgent referral is typically downstream of acuity and is itself part of the process that lengthens the visit; it lies on the causal path from severity to duration rather than being a common cause of an independent treatment. Adjusting for it as a confounder would be an error.

per_column.name: counseling_complexity
per_column.rationale: Amount of counseling is a candidate clinical factor whose effect on duration is being attributed; more counseling directly consumes visit time.

per_column.name: multimorbidity_signal
per_column.rationale: Multimorbidity plausibly causes both the intensity of clinical activity (counseling, procedures) and longer duration, making it a genuine common cause not named in the query.

per_column.name: multimorbidity_or_polypharmacy
per_column.rationale: Near-duplicate of multimorbidity_signal; same confounding role, redundant. Common cause of clinical intensity and duration.

judge.rationale: The set does set up a causal estimation: it supplies candidate treatments (procedure_performed, counseling_complexity) and several plausible common causes of both treatment and duration (visit_type_category, condition_acuity, multimorbidity). Crucially these confounders were surfaced from the clinical content rather than copied from the query, which only said 'clinical factors' and 'visit duration' — demonstrating the capability under test. Weaknesses: admission_or_urgent_referral is more a mediator/outcome-adjacent variable than a confounder (adjusting for it would bias attribution), and multimorbidity is duplicated, inflating apparent coverage. Overall a moderately strong but imperfect realisation of causal attribution.
